key_insight: Deep learning and multimodal ultrasound models showed promising internal prediction of spontaneous preterm birth, but external performance dropped sharply, highlighting limited transportability.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests mid-trimester cervical ultrasound may help risk stratification, but current models are not ready for reliable real-world use without further validation.
method: Prospective development on the GARBH-Ini cohort
Compared texture-based, clinical, deep-learning, and multimodal models
Externally validated on an independent cohort scanned with a different ultrasound machine
evidence_signal: Best model achieved AUC 0.71 internally but only 0.52 externally, with estimates imprecise due to few preterm birth cases.
watch_item: External generalizability is limited, likely due to heterogeneity in preterm birth and scanner/site differences, so implementation should be cautious.
paper_title: Development and external validation of deep learning models for spontaneous preterm birth prediction from mid-trimester cervical ultrasound
